messages:
acme-admin: Hey team — after our cluster NetPolicy rollout agent DaemonSet can't register with Redwood Private. Agent pods start but never show healthy, and control plane calls fail in the logs with DNS/TLS errors. Rolled back but want root cause.

maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the agent pod logs and the NetPolicy you applied? Quick checks: can pods resolve the control plane host and reach 443?

acme-admin: Logs (trimmed):
```
I0321 10:04:12.345678 1 main.go:145] starting redwood-agent
E0321 10:04:13.112233 1 net.go:87] dial tcp: lookup control-plane.redwoodops.net on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host
E0321 10:04:13.112250 1 agent.go:201] registration failed: context deadline exceeded
```
We also tried curl from a debug pod and nslookup times out. NetPolicy we applied (simplified):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
```

ashok (eng-sre): That policy will block ALL egress by default. Two common hits: 1) blocking UDP/53 to kube-dns so pods can't resolve control-plane host, 2) blocking TCP/443 outbound to redwood endpoints. Can you run a couple quick repro commands from a busybox/curl pod?

mike (eng-infra): Run: `kubectl run -it --rm --image=radial/busyboxplus:curl debug -- /bin/sh` then inside pod:
- `nslookup control-plane.redwoodops.net 10.96.0.10`
- `dig +short @10.96.0.10 control-plane.redwoodops.net`
- `curl -v https://control-plane.redwoodops.net/health --max-time 10`

acme-admin: Ran those. nslookup/ dig -> no response (timeouts). curl -> `connect: connection timed out`. tcpdump on node shows no UDP to 10.96.0.10 from pod IP.

maya (support): Sounds like NetPolicy egress deny is active for the agent pods. NetworkPolicies are whitelists for allowed traffic. If you need a quick workaround to confirm: add an allow egress policy for the agent namespace to kube-dns and to Redwood control-plane IPs/ranges on port 443. Example (very small):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-agent-egress-dns-and-control
  namespace: redwood-agent-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kube-system: "true"   # kube-dns namespace label differs per distro; use actual selector
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 34.120.0.0/14    # example Redwood control plane CIDR — verify with Redwood
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

ashok (eng-sre): A few notes:
- NetworkPolicy can't match FQDNs; you need IPs or allow blanket 0.0.0.0/0:443 if you can't enumerate.
- For managed DNS (CoreDNS), allow UDP/53 to the kube-dns service ClusterIP, or allow egress to the node-local resolver depending on your cluster setup.
- If you use Cilium or Calico, there are features (e.g., calico egress networkpolicy, cilium egress policies, or egress gateway) to limit to domains.

mike (eng-infra): We tried a quick allow to 0.0.0.0/0:443 and UDP/53 to 10.96.0.10 and agent pods started registering. Agent logs now show successful TLS handshake.

acme-admin: Confirmed — after applying the allow policy agents came up and registered within ~30s. Thanks.

maya (support): Great. For long term, recommend: 1) enumerate Redwood control plane IP ranges we use (we can provide the current list of IP ranges to allow), 2) prefer allowing to namespace/service selector for kube-dns instead of 0.0.0.0/0 where possible, 3) if you need hostname-based egress allowlists look into an egress proxy or Cilium/DNS-aware egress features.

ashok (eng-sre): Also watch for probes: kubelet liveness/readiness probes may need hostNetwork or explicit NetPolicy allowances for node <-> pod comms, and node egress to registries (for image pulls) if you enforce egress.

acme-admin: One follow-up — agent TLS failures originally showed `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` for one attempt after rollback. We traced that to our cluster intercepting outbound TLS via MITM proxy for inspection; after whitelisting control-plane host the agent used CA pinning and succeeded. So two separate factors: NetPolicy blocking DNS/443 and outbound TLS inspection.

mike (eng-infra): Filed internal change to add a documented NetPolicy snippet for Redwood private deployments in our infra repo. We'll keep outbound to Redwood control plane and kube-dns allowed.

deploy-bot: Deployment redwood-agent v1.2.3 reverted -> rolled forward (confirmed new NetPolicy applied)

maya (support): I'll document this incident and send the recommended NetPolicy example and the Redwood control plane IP ranges to your infra slack channel. If you want, we can schedule a quick runbook review to avoid surprises during future NetPolicy rollouts. :thumbsup:

acme-admin: Yes please — appreciate the quick triage.
